title: TLS: Fix issuerDN for created certificates

timeline.message:
TLS: Fix issuerDN for created certificates

Certificate chains require subjectCert.issuerDN = issuerCert.subjectDN.
Each adjacent certificate must satisfy this relationship, or else they
fail certificate chain validation.

CertGenUtils was setting subjectCert.issuerDN = issuerCert.issuerDN.
That was incorrect. If the issuerCert was for a root CA, then issuerCert
had the same value for issuerCert.subjectDN = issuerCert.issuerDN, and
it was not possible to detect the bug.

For testing, use a subordinate CA to create a TLS certificate. A
subordinate CA has different values for its issuerCert.subjectDN !=
issuerCert.issuerDN. When the TLS certificate is created, it becomes
possible to assert subjectCert.issuerDN = issuerCert.subjectDN for the
TLS certificate.

Closes #69403
timeline.author: Justin Cranford

Each adjacent certificate must satisfy this relationship, or else they
fail certificate chain validation.

CertGenUtils was setting subjectCert.issuerDN = issuerCert.issuerDN.
That was incorrect. If the issuerCert was for a root CA, then issuerCert

subordinate CA has different values for its issuerCert.subjectDN !=

Closes #69403

We generally prefer to use Hamcrest style assertions (although we also have a lot of older code that uses the standard JUnit assertion style).
Matcher-based assertions give much better failure messages which has an enormous benefit over a large codebase like ES (the person triaging a failure has typically not seen the test before, and the better the assertion failure message is, the easier & quicker it is to resolve).

timeline.message:
Update: Address PR comments, add PKIX DN checking

Updated the PR to address the forbidden API and code style comments.
Verified the changes with these commands:
- ./gradlew :x-pack:plugin:security:cli:forbiddenApisTest
- ./gradlew :x-pack:plugin:security:cli:checkstyleTest

Added a helper method to call PKIX cert chain validation too. Issue
#77828 is specific to DN chaining, and some simple assertions in
the unit test cover the fix. However, PKIX/SunJSSE TrustManager does a
more thorough job validating DN chaining, as well as additional
chaining checks like signatures, SKI/AKI, BC/KU/EKU, and more.
